subject: Retention matrix and customer exception runbook - Mediq request
messages:
From: Rebecca Lane <r.lane@mediq.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Tenant-specific log retention - short question

Hi Nikhil,

We have an upcoming audit and our security team is pushing for tenant-scoped retention of operational logs for a specific Mediq regulated product. We need to retain API request metadata and authentication/audit traces for 180 days for one tenant (no request/response payloads or user-submitted content).

Can Redwood support a customer-specific retention override for hosted customers (i.e., keep certain log classes on-platform for longer than the default 30/90d windows)? If not, what recommended pattern would you suggest that still lets us demonstrate control and evidence to our auditors (SOC 2 / CAIQ / SIG)?

I've attached our audit request (MediQ_Audit_Request_2026.pdf) and a CSV with what the audit team expects (mediq_retention_requirements.csv). This is time-sensitive — audit kickoff next week.

Thanks,
Rebecca Lane
Security Program Manager, Mediq Health
Attachments: Mediq_Audit_Request_2026.pdf, mediq_retention_requirements.csv
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Rebecca Lane <r.lane@mediq.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant-specific log retention - short question

Hi Rebecca — thanks for the note and the materials, and sorry for the quick turnaround ask on your end. High level: we can solve this two ways depending on the exact log classes you need and the deployment mode you prefer.

Option A (native per-tenant retention): we have a tenant-labeling mechanism that can extend retention for metadata/audit traces, but there are product constraints for hosted tiers — longer retention for hosted customers is possible but requires an operational exception and has cost/SL implications (and we usually reserve it for Dedicated customers).

Option B (export & custody): configure continuous export of the required log classes (auth, request metadata, audit traces) to a customer-controlled S3 bucket with SSE-KMS. You retain control, we provide signed manifests and delivery proofs. This pattern is what most customers use when they need cryptographic custody or longer retention without a Dedicated deployment.

To help us scope the work, can you confirm: 1) exact log classes (for example: request headers & durations, auth success/fail events, routing/audit traces — explicitly exclude request/response bodies if applicable), 2) whether Mediq will provide an S3 bucket (or want us to host exports temporarily), and 3) whether you need an attestation for SOC 2/CAIQ or a contractual amendment?

If helpful I can jump on a 30-min call today or tomorrow — available 1:30–3pm PT today or 10–12pm PT tomorrow.

—Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — Developer-first inference runtime
From: Rebecca Lane <r.lane@mediq.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T11:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant-specific log retention - short question

Thanks Nikhil — quick clarifications:
- Log classes: we need API request metadata (timestamp, request id, tenant id, headers excluding sensitive headers, latency) and authentication/audit traces (token issuance, refresh, invalidation, admin api calls). We explicitly DO NOT want request/response bodies or user content retained.
- We will provide an S3 bucket with organization-managed KMS keys.
- The audit team wants: evidence of retention policy, delivery proofs (manifests), and a short attestation that data was exported and retained for the requested window. A contractual amendment is preferable but not mandatory for the first pass.

Can you confirm if the exported files include a manifest with checksums? If Redwood can provide a signed manifest on export and a per-batch delivery signature, that should satisfy compliance.

Appreciate the quick help — if you can send a proposed runbook or matrix that maps log class -> retention location -> control evidence, that would move us forward.

Rebecca
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Tenant-specific log retention - initial approach and suggested wording

Folks — looping in a short technical/compliance summary to use in the runbook and SIG/CAIQ answers. Notes below are draft language we can include in evidence pack.

1) Capability: For hosted customers, Redwood supports continuous export of scoped operational telemetry (request metadata and auth/audit traces) to a customer-provided S3 bucket. Export batches include a gzipped NDJSON file and a signed manifest (SHA256 checksums + batch id). We can also retain an internal delivery log for 90 days.

2) Native retention override: Per-tenant on-platform retention overrides for hosted tenants are available but on an exception basis. They require an operational review and will usually be included only under a Dedicated plan or a paid exception for hosted. On-platform retention beyond 90 days for hosted customers increases exposure and is gated by legal/compliance.

3) Controls & encryption: Exports support SSE-KMS with customer-managed keys. We include timestamps, batch ids, and per-file checksums. Delivery proofs are signed with Redwood KMS and can be included in an evidence bundle for audits.

Suggested SIG/CAIQ phrasing (concise): "Redwood exports scoped operational telemetry to customer-controlled storage. Export batches include checksums and signed manifests; customers may retain exported logs under their own retention policy. Native per-tenant retention beyond the platform default is available via an exception or Dedicated deployment."

Action items: Marissa — can you build the mapping matrix (log class -> export topic -> manifest example) into retention_matrix_v1.xlsx and produce a short runbook. Karthik — we should propose a commercial amendment for the exception path (fee + SLA update). Nikhil — coordinate with Rebecca on S3 details and timeline.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-08-10T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Tenant-specific log retention - commercial notes

Quick commercial note — for the exception path (native on-platform >90d) we recommend a 12-month amendment with a fixed monthly fee to cover storage + indexing costs and an SLA that limits immutable retention changes to scheduled maintenance windows. For the export technique there is no platform fee but there is a setup/enablement charge and an ongoing export bandwidth/storage advisory.

Propose: add a line to the order form for "Customer-specific retention & export runbook" and include a one-off enablement fee (E) + monthly retention surcharge (M). I can get exact numbers once Marissa outlines the runbook scope. Deal: DEAL-8732.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions Sales, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-08-11T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant-specific log retention - runbook and next steps

Hi Rebecca — thanks for the clarifications and patience. Attached is an initial retention matrix and a short runbook (retention_matrix_v1.xlsx) that maps the log classes you specified to an export-based solution we can stand up quickly. Summary below plus next steps:

Summary:
- Scope: API request metadata + auth/audit traces only. Excludes request/response bodies.
- Implementation: continuous export to your S3 bucket (SSE-KMS, customer-managed keys). Files delivered hourly as gzipped NDJSON + signed manifest (SHA256).
- Evidence: we will provide sample signed manifests, a delivery manifest index, and a short attestation statement confirming delivery and retention timeline for exported batches.
- Timeline: export enablement and evidence bundle for hosted customers: target 7 business days from S3 access and PO/enablement sign-off. Native on-platform retention >90d: requires contract amendment and operational review (estimated 3–6 weeks).

Next steps:
1) Please share S3 bucket ARN and KMS key principal to allow Redwood write permissions.
2) Confirm whether Mediq prefers the export-only route or wants Redwood to escalate the native retention exception path.
3) If you want a contractual amendment, I can spin a one-page addendum (Karthik / Legal will route).

DocuSign link for the enablement addendum (optional): https://redwood.app/ds/12345

Attachments: retention_matrix_v1.xlsx (matrix + manifest example), sample_manifest.json (inline in workbook).

Happy to hop on the call if useful — Nikhil and Neha are on copy.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Compliance Program Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: retention_matrix_v1.xlsx
